narr: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of northeast Illinois during the afternoon and evening of July 8th producing heavy rain. One thunderstorm slowly moved across central Cook County and Chicago in the late evening producing torrential rain and flash flooding.
ev: Street and viaduct flooding were reported in numerous areas in central Chicago generally between Interstate 55 to the south, North Avenue to the north and Cicero Avenue to the west. Water rescues were reported at Western Avenue and Ogden Avenue and at Kinzie Street and Ashland Avenue. At least two viaducts were flooded in North Lawndale and a car was stalled in flood waters on Roosevelt Road just east of California Avenue. The local lanes of Interstate 90 were closed due to flooding between 18th Street and 31st Street. In Garfield Park, a car was submerged in flood waters on West Fulton Street; At least 3 garages were flooded with flood waters rushing like a river down an alley and multiple basements were flooded. Near the Chicago Loop, street flooding was reported along with a viaduct flooded and a photo showed a few inches of standing water at Hubbard's Cave on Interstate 90/94. An estimated 200 basements were flooded in the Near West Side. Street flooding was reported in West Town along with a few basements flooded. In Cicero, a few inches of standing water were reported on streets and sidewalks.||An automated rain gauge east of Garfield Park reported 5.12 inches of rain in 90 minutes from 19:55 CST to 21:25 CST with a storm total of 5.45 inches. A personal weather station west of the Loop reported 3.81 inches in about 2 hours at 21:43 CST.
